thread:
ashley: Heads-up — we should converge on a simpler continuation protocol so Python/TS/Go SDKs can share transport & retry behavior. Thoughts?

tomas: +1. Current tokens carry too much server-state; makes client retry semantics fragile.

priya: Agree. What if tokens are purely opaque cursor + checksum? Server can validate, clients just replay the token. Keeps server flexible while keeping client simple.

kevin: We also need to account for resumable streaming. Cursors are fine for paged endpoints, but streaming needs sequence ids + offset to resume mid-stream.

ashley: Proposal sketch: two token modes —
- cursor: opaque string for paged APIs
- session: ephemeral session id + offset for streaming
Both are opaque to clients. Server decides which to return.

priya: Edge cases: cache/prefix optimization. If tokens change shape often during rollouts, clients relying on token stability break. We should document stable prefixes or a version byte.

ashley: Good call. Add a 1-byte version prefix in the token so we can migrate formats without breaking older SDKs.

kevin: For retries, clients should be allowed to retry idempotent endpoints. How does server tell client "do not replay"?

tomas: Either an explicit header (Retry-Allowed: false) or an error body sentinel. Header is simpler for SDKs to check before retry.

priya: Header sounds right. Also return Retry-After when we want backoff from server side.

ashley: SDK retry policy defaults: exponential + full jitter, base_delay=100ms, max_attempts=3, max_delay=5s. Make it per-route configurable.

kevin: We should standardize a minimal RetryPolicy shape across languages. Example: { maxAttempts, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, retryOn: ["timeout","5xx"] }

priya: Quick prototype (JS):
```js
// minimal API shape we want across SDKs
const retryPolicy = {
  maxAttempts: 3,
  baseDelayMs: 100,
  maxDelayMs: 5000,
  retryOn: ["ETIMEDOUT", "ECONNRESET", "5xx"],
};
```

ashley: And Python:
```py
# same idea in py SDK
retry_policy = dict(
    max_attempts=3,
    base_delay_ms=100,
    max_delay_ms=5000,
    retry_on=["timeout", "connection_reset", "5xx"],
)
```

tomas: For transport choices: prefer HTTP/2 with streaming support where available, fallback to HTTP/1.1 long-poll for environments that don't support it. SDK transport adapter should abstract that away.

kevin: Yes — transport adapter interface: send(request) -> response stream/iterable. Implementations: http2, http1, local-mock (for tests). Keep it small.

priya: One more: partial response / partial-commit semantics. If server accepts some commit before final token, how does client know? Add a small response header: X-Continuation-Status: partial|complete.

ashley: Nice. So summarizing proposal:
- token types: cursor (paged) and session (streaming) with 1-byte format version prefix
- server signals retryability via Retry-Allowed header + optional Retry-After
- standard RetryPolicy shape implemented in all SDKs (defaults as above)
- transport adapter abstraction (http2/http1/mock)
- small headers for continuation status and migration friendliness

kevin: Does this cover resumability across different server versions? The version byte + semantic headers should. If server returns an unknown version byte, SDK should surface an error hinting at upgrade.

ashley: Implementation plan:
- Priya: draft a minimal JSON spec of token shape + headers (PR) — owner: priya
- Tomas: implement RetryPolicy + transport adapter interface in TS SDK — owner: tomas
- Kevin: mirror transport adapter & session token bits in Go SDK — owner: kevin
- Ashley: python SDK defaults + docs + migration notes — owner: ashley

ci-bot: automated-note: updated RFC draft pushed to https://redwood.example.com/rfc/continuation-protocol (link) :white_check_mark:

tomas: I'll open a tiny design PR for the TS adapter today, ping me for review.

priya: I'll put the token spec in docs + add examples for upgrade path.

kevin: I'll prototype session resume for streaming, want to test with http2 multiplexing.

ashley: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups in #eng-platform — tag me if you need design sign-off. :rocket:
